/-!
# Smallest index $k > n$ such that $(p_k+p_{k+1})/(p_n+p_{n+1})$ is an integer $\ge 2$

*References:*
- [A167918](https://oeis.org/A167918)-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA167918

/-- $P(i)$ is the $i$-th prime, 1-indexed. -/
noncomputable def P (i : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.nth Nat.Prime (i - 1)

/-- $S(i) = p_i + p_{i+1}$. -/
noncomputable def S (i : ℕ) : ℕ := P i + P (i + 1)

/-- Smallest index $k > n$ such that $S(n) \mid S(k)$. -/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then 0
  else sInf { k : ℕ | k > n ∧ S n ∣ S k }

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 0 := by rfl

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma P_1 : P 1 = 2 := Nat.nth_prime_zero_eq_two

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma P_2 : P 2 = 3 := Nat.nth_prime_one_eq_three

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma P_3 : P 3 = 5 := Nat.nth_prime_two_eq_five

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma P_4 : P 4 = 7 := Nat.nth_prime_three_eq_seven

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma P_5 : P 5 = 11 := Nat.nth_prime_four_eq_eleven

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma P_6 : P 6 = 13 := by
  dsimp [P]
  have h : (13 : ℕ).Prime := by decide
  exact Nat.nth_count h

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma P_7 : P 7 = 17 := by
  dsimp [P]
  have h : (17 : ℕ).Prime := by decide
  exact Nat.nth_count h

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma P_8 : P 8 = 19 := by
  dsimp [P]
  have h : (19 : ℕ).Prime := by decide
  exact Nat.nth_count h

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma S_1 : S 1 = 5 := by dsimp [S]; rw [P_1, P_2]

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma S_2 : S 2 = 8 := by dsimp [S]; rw [P_2, P_3]

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma S_3 : S 3 = 12 := by dsimp [S]; rw [P_3, P_4]

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma S_4 : S 4 = 18 := by dsimp [S]; rw [P_4, P_5]

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma S_5 : S 5 = 24 := by dsimp [S]; rw [P_5, P_6]

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma S_6 : S 6 = 30 := by dsimp [S]; rw [P_6, P_7]

@[category API, AMS 11]
lemma S_7 : S 7 = 36 := by dsimp [S]; rw [P_7, P_8]

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 6 := by
  have h_least : IsLeast { k : ℕ | k > 1 ∧ S 1 ∣ S k } 6 := by
    constructor
    · simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      refine ⟨by decide, ?_⟩
      rw [S_1, S_6]
      decide
    · intro k hk
      simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at hk
      by_contra! h
      have hk_gt := hk.1
      interval_cases k
      · have hdiv := hk.2
        rw [S_1, S_2] at hdiv
        revert hdiv; decide
      · have hdiv := hk.2
        rw [S_1, S_3] at hdiv
        revert hdiv; decide
      · have hdiv := hk.2
        rw [S_1, S_4] at hdiv
        revert hdiv; decide
      · have hdiv := hk.2
        rw [S_1, S_5] at hdiv
        revert hdiv; decide
  have ha1 : a 1 = sInf { k : ℕ | k > 1 ∧ S 1 ∣ S k } := by
    unfold a; split <;> [omega; rfl]
  rw [ha1, h_least.csInf_eq]

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 5 := by
  have h_least : IsLeast { k : ℕ | k > 2 ∧ S 2 ∣ S k } 5 := by
    constructor
    · simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      refine ⟨by decide, ?_⟩
      rw [S_2, S_5]
      decide
    · intro k hk
      simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at hk
      by_contra! h
      have hk_gt := hk.1
      interval_cases k
      · have hdiv := hk.2
        rw [S_2, S_3] at hdiv
        revert hdiv; decide
      · have hdiv := hk.2
        rw [S_2, S_4] at hdiv
        revert hdiv; decide
  have ha2 : a 2 = sInf { k : ℕ | k > 2 ∧ S 2 ∣ S k } := by
    unfold a; split <;> [omega; rfl]
  rw [ha2, h_least.csInf_eq]

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 5 := by
  have h_least : IsLeast { k : ℕ | k > 3 ∧ S 3 ∣ S k } 5 := by
    constructor
    · simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      refine ⟨by decide, ?_⟩
      rw [S_3, S_5]
      decide
    · intro k hk
      simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at hk
      by_contra! h
      have hk_gt := hk.1
      interval_cases k
      · have hdiv := hk.2
        rw [S_3, S_4] at hdiv
        revert hdiv; decide
  have ha3 : a 3 = sInf { k : ℕ | k > 3 ∧ S 3 ∣ S k } := by
    unfold a; split <;> [omega; rfl]
  rw [ha3, h_least.csInf_eq]

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 7 := by
  have h_least : IsLeast { k : ℕ | k > 4 ∧ S 4 ∣ S k } 7 := by
    constructor
    · simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      refine ⟨by decide, ?_⟩
      rw [S_4, S_7]
      decide
    · intro k hk
      simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at hk
      by_contra! h
      have hk_gt := hk.1
      interval_cases k
      · have hdiv := hk.2
        rw [S_4, S_5] at hdiv
        revert hdiv; decide
      · have hdiv := hk.2
        rw [S_4, S_6] at hdiv
        revert hdiv; decide
  have ha4 : a 4 = sInf { k : ℕ | k > 4 ∧ S 4 ∣ S k } := by
    unfold a; split <;> [omega; rfl]
  rw [ha4, h_least.csInf_eq]

/--
Conjecture: $f(n, k) = 2$ for infinitely many cases, where $k = a(n)$.

No hypothesis on the existence of $a(n)$ is needed: if no suitable $k > n$ exists then
$a(n) = 0$ and $S(0) = 4 < 2 S(n)$, so such $n$ cannot be witnesses.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture1 (M : ℕ) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, n ≥ M ∧ n > 0 ∧ S (a n) = 2 * S n := by
  sorry

/--
Open problem: Whether the ratio $f(n, k)$ is bounded, where $k = a(n)$.

We assume $a(n) \ne 0$ (i.e., that a suitable $k > n$ always exists), as `sInf` evaluates to $0$
on an empty set.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture2 (ha : ∀ n > 0, a n ≠ 0) :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n > 0 → S (a n) / S n ≤ C := by
  sorry


end OeisA167918

findings.description: Lines 216–218 assert that, assuming the sequence is defined everywhere, there exists a uniform bound C. There is no `answer(sorry)` slot: the declaration commits to the affirmative answer, whereas the source poses boundedness as an unresolved yes/no question. A negative resolution of that question would not establish this declaration, even under its totality hypothesis.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A167918, comment (5): “Open problems: (a) is f(n,k) bounded, (b) which integer values for f(n,k) are "possible".” Unlike comments (1) and (2), this does not conjecture an affirmative answer. Read through the official OEIS data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A167/A167918.seq.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an open propositional answer slot. For example, boundedness over the defined terms can be stated as `theorem conjecture2 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n > 0 → a n ≠ 0 → S (a n) / S n ≤ C := by sorry`. If retaining the current global-totality presupposition, make that conditional version an explicit `answer(sorry)` question rather than asserting its affirmative side.

reformulations.difference: The minimization predicate uses `k > n ∧ S n ∣ S k`, without explicitly requiring the quotient to be an integer at least 2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For 0 < n < k, the indexed primes give 0 < S n < S k. Consequently, divisibility is equivalent to the existence of a natural q ≥ 2 satisfying S k = q * S n. Thus the minimization predicates agree. The scratch file proves this equivalence and verifies that a nonzero `a n` is the least admissible index.

reformulations.difference: Infinitely many ratio-2 cases are expressed as arbitrarily large positive n satisfying the cross-multiplied equality at `a n`, without a separate existence hypothesis for `a n`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive n, S n ≥ 5, whereas S 0 = 4, so the default a n = 0 cannot satisfy the equality. Every witness therefore has a genuine least admissible index. Conversely, any later index with ratio 2 must be the least admissible one: all admissible ratios are integers ≥ 2, and S is strictly increasing. Unboundedness of the witness indices is equivalent to infinitude. The complete equivalence with infinitely many positive n admitting a later k with rational ratio 2 was proved in `Review167918.conjecture1_source_form`.

reformulations.difference: The boundedness predicate uses natural-number division and a natural-number bound rather than a real-valued ratio and real bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the displayed totality hypothesis, `a n` satisfies S n ∣ S (a n), and S n is positive. Natural division is therefore exact. A natural bound supplies a real bound, and any real bound can be enlarged to a natural one. This equivalence of the boundedness predicates was proved in `Review167918.boundedness_nat_iff_real`; it does not resolve the separate missing-answer-slot defect.

sources_consulted: OEIS A167918, complete entry via its official data repository: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A167/A167918.seq
Checked-out Mathlib: Mathlib/Data/Nat/Nth.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Prime/Defs.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Prime/Nth.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Prime/Infinite.lean; Mathlib/Order/Lattice/Nat.lean.
review.notes: Checked all definitions, P_1–P_8, S_1–S_7, a_0–a_4, and both research declarations. An independent executable prime search reproduced all 62 OEIS data terms. The scratch file /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles, and the reported equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependency. The main OEIS HTML endpoints returned a Cloudflare challenge, so the complete entry was read through the official OEIS data repository. The source still records the relevant questions as open. Its separate conjecture that the sequence is infinite explains the file's explicit totality presupposition; that modelling choice is not counted as a second confirmed defect.

not_demonstrated.reason: The reported defect is that OEIS asks whether the ratios are bounded, while Lean asserts boundedness under a totality hypothesis. This source-versus-statement discrepancy supplies neither a trivial proof nor a counterexample to the boundedness assertion itself. Proving or refuting its exact type would require resolving substantive mathematics; invoking the imported sorry-backed declaration would not be an honest demonstration.

submission.summary: No short mathematical demonstration is available for the reported missing-answer-slot defect. No trivial-proof file was created.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole finding concerns committing to an affirmative answer rather than leaving a question open, not a degeneracy making the formalized proposition trivially true or false.

submission.summary: Added `answer(sorry) ↔` so boundedness remains an open yes/no question. Replaced the global totality assumption with a per-index `a n ≠ 0` guard and updated the explanatory docstring. No other declarations were changed. The requested compile succeeded with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
